findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

A single wiping cloth was observed left on a counter and moist with food residues. The PIC was shown and instructed to store the wiping cloths between uses in the available sani buckets to prevent pathogenic growths. The rag was moved to a sani bucket to correct.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The gasket of the mini cooler in a cabinet at the coffee bar is observed to be in disrepair. This was shown to the PIC. Ensure that this gasket is replaced. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The sliders of the doors on the front display cases. 
2. The walk-in cooler shelves. 
3. The bottom of the sheet pan storage rack in the bakery area. 

These were discussed with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ice cream scoops fully submerged in the running well. CORRECTED- the well was emptied and cleaned, and the scoops were brought to the dish area for ware washing. Ensure scoops and all food contact surfaces are stored with the handles ABOVE the water to prevent bare hand contamination of the food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed sausage in the kitchen’s under counter cooler to bear the following dates: 2/26 and 3/3. Both of these dates are past the seven day date marking requirements for temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods. CORRECTED- the sausage was voluntarily discarded by kitchen staff. Ensure dates are removed and proper ware washing ensues for all food contact surfaces. Ensure all TCS foods are used or discarded within seven days- the day of preparation/ thawing counts as day one.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [Pf]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed stir spoons at the barista station in a mixed orientation. CORRECTED- education occurred on in use utensils storage with the PIC. Ensure all in-use utensils are stored in a manner that will prevent bare hand contamination of the food contact surface.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed gaskets at the double door standing cooler (unit #2) in the kitchen to be fraying. All nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that equipment is maintained and in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed pasta salad on an ice bath to be probed at 49F. CORRECTED- person in charge (PIC) stated the serving had been sitting out for approximately one hour, so the item was moved into a cooler. Education about ice baths occurred with PIC. Ensure items moved out during busy periods are either; held at or below 41F, are in an ice bath which surrounds the bottom and sides of the container, or time as control for food safety (TAC) is used.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) items without date marking (caramel iced latte, milk, and sour cream). CORRECTED- the caramel iced latte is not currently being used, but education about date marking occurred. Milk and sour cream were both opened or prepared yesterday, and were marked with the corresponding date. Ensure all TCS items are date marked with the date they are opened, prepared, or thawed, and used or discarded within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed insect control device over foods in hot holding. CORRECTED- PIC moved the light away from food storage. Ensure all pest control devices are installed away from areas of food storage and preparation to prevent insects from contaminating food.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple wet sanitizer cloths being stored on counters in both the bar area and the kitchen. CORRECTED- education occurred with PIC and staff. Ensure wet sanitizer cloths are stored in a sanitizer solution when not in use to prevent the growth of pathogens on the cloth.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector observed Certified Food Protection Manager’s (CFPM/CFM) Allergen awareness training to be expired. Allergen awareness training must be maintained and renewed every 3 years for facility’s CFMs. Ensure CFMs receive Allergen Awareness training by ANSI accredited program by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two different employees donning gloves without washing hands. CORRECTED- Inspector educated employees about the need to wash hands before donning gloves, and they washed hands before putting on new pairs of gloves. Ensure employees wash hands before donning gloves and having contact with food.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee use the hand washing sink behind the service counter to clean slushee catch tray. CORRECTED- Inspector informed employee that hand washing sinks should not be used to clean dishes. Ensure that designated hand washing sinks are used only for hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine near the triple sink was observed not to be dispensing sanitizer. Inspector notified the person in charge, who called and put in a service order. Use the triple sink to sanitize by hand until the machine is serviced and observed to dispensing the appropriate amount of sanitizer.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The following food contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
1) The container holding drink stirring spoons at the cafe station- CORRECTED- employee took container and spoons to be cleaned and sanitized.
2) Ice baffles were observed to have slight mold. A follow up is scheduled on 07/28/25 to ensure the ice baffles are clean to sight and touch.

Ensure that all food contact surfaces are routinely cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed pasta salad and cut melon in prep cooler without date marking. CORRECTED- inspector notified the person in charge, and they stated the items were both prepared yesterday. The operator put dates on both items. Ensure that all items prepared at the facility and being held for more than twenty four hours are marked with the date of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed several items (mushroom, gravy, mixed peppers, sauteed onions, chimi sc, and cream cheese) to be stored and used past the 7 day date requirement. CORRECTED- person in charge was notified and voluntarily discarded items that had been prepared over seven days ago. Ensure that all items are used or discarded within seven days of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed gaskets at the double door standing cooler in the kitchen to be cracked. Discussed observations with the person in charge. Ensure that equipment is maintained and in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Several non-food contact surfaces were observed to contain significant amounts of dust, ice, or food debris:
1) The sliding doors at the ice cream display freezer and bakery display freezer contained food debris.
2) The ice cream display freezer contained a significant amount of ice accumulation along the freezer walls. Routinely defrost freezer and remove ice accumulation during cleaning.
3) A significant amount of dust was observed on the walk in cooler fans.
4) Shelving unit across from triple sink contained rust and some dust accumulation. Remove shelves to be cleaned and sealed or replaced. 

Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust or debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to leave the kitchen wearing gloves, retrieve soap, place it at the handsink, and return to handling clean dishes without removing/changing gloves or washing hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PICs, who will review handwashing with employees. Employees must wash hands after any activity that may have contaminated hands (such as leaving the kitchen), and before handling clean equipment and utensils.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: No soap was available at the front handwashing sink upon inspectors arrival. Upon request, an employee provided soap to the handsink. Ensure soap is always available at all handwashing sinks.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Sanitizer buckets throughout the facility were observed with no measurable quat concentration. Upon further investigation, it was determined that sanitizer is not being dispensed from the wall-mounted dispenser at the proper concentration. Staff will mix sanitizer by hand and use test strips to check concentration until the wall-mounted dispenser is fixed. Use test strips regularly to monitor sanitizer concentrations. Inspector will follow up to verify that the wall-mounted dispenser has been repaired and is functioning properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall have a concentration of 200-400ppm as indicated on the manufacturer’s label. [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Muffins and scones were observed prepackaged on the service counter without any labeling present. Ensure foods that are prepackaged in advance of sale are labeled with the information below.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11 (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; and (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Small portion cups of loose leaf tea, sealed tea bags, and containers of chai are stored under the barista prep/rinse sink. Store foods away from potential sources of contamination. Discussed storage in other cabinets or in plastic containers with lids.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.12 FOOD may not be stored (I) Under other sources of contamination. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking sealing the three compartment sink and drainboards to the wall is cracked, creating a surface that is not smooth or easily cleanable. Recaulk the three compartment sink and drainboards to the wall so the transition is smooth, easily cleanable, and cracks/crevices are eliminated.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Kitchen sanitizer bucket was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- Sanitizer bucket was refilled from the wall-mounted dispenser and observed at 200ppm quat.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration of 200-400 ppm quat (based on manufacturer’s label). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in the prep cooler were observed at 48-60F (probed). Out of temperature foods include sliced and diced tomatoes, pasta salad, sliced and shredded cheeses, cut melon, cooked onions, chicken salad, and sliced turkey. CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
The prep cooler is not functioning properly to maintain foods at 41F or below. Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. A repair tech was on-site for a different cooler and will look at the prep cooler. Ensure coolers are functioning properly to hold foods at 41F or below. Conduct routine temperature checks to catch malfunctions and provide timelines when a cooler is found out of temperature.
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
A cocktail spoon was observed in the basin of the kitchen handsink upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- PIC removed the spoon upon inspector’s request. Ensure handsinks are used only for handwashing, and are maintained clear and accessible to facilitate frequent handwashing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Pink and brown mold accumulation observed on the baffle of the kitchen ice machine. CORRECTED- PIC cleaned ice machine baffle.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Plastic spoons in the kitchen were observed stored mix direction (some with spoon/food contact end up, others with handle up). Ensure utensils are stored so only the handles are touched. CORRECTED- PIC discarded the spoons that were stored food contact end up. 
4-904.11: (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: The three compartment sink and drainboards are not sealed to the wall. Clean wall to remove existing caulk and mold, then reseal the 3 compartment sink to the wall.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
There are small holes in the wall behind the kitchen handsink (from removed soap/paper towel dispensers, etc). Fill holes so the wall is smooth and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Reporting agreements are not on file for two employees. CORRECTED- PIC had employees review and sign reporting agreements. Ensure all new employees are educated on foodborne illnesses and symptoms. Keep signed reporting agreements on file.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
The ice bin at the barista counter was observed uncovered. CORRECTED- Ice bin was closed. Keep ice bin closed when not in use.
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The three compartment sink and drainboards are not sealed to the wall. Clean wall to remove existing caulk and mold, then reseal the 3 compartment sink to the wall.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Pink and brown mold accumulation observed on the baffle of the kitchen ice machine. CORRECTED: PIC cleaned ice machine baffle.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
1) Heavy whipping cream, half and half, dairy milk, and non-dairy milks throughout the facility (in barista coolers, kitchen cooler #6, and the walk-in cooler) observed without date markings. Label containers with the date opened to ensure that they are used or discarded within 7 days of opening. Containers were labeled with the dates they were opened.
2) Two open gallons of fat-free milk (in a barista cooler and the walk-in) observed with manufacturer use-by dates of 7/25. One container of heavy whipping cream in the walk in observed with an open-date of 6/26. Past-date items were voluntarily discarded.
3-501.17: (A) Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Spray bottle of blue liquid observed near the barista handsink without any labeling. Staff labeled bottle to indicate contents (window cleaner).
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
Ponding water observed in the bottoms of both barista coolers. Repair to eliminate ponding water.
5-403.12: Condensate drainage and other non-SEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PIC’s allergen training certificate expired earlier this year. Ensure CFMs complete ANSI-approved allergen training. Keep certificates on file.
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07  Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Multiple priority violations were observed during this inspection: handwashing, bare hand contact, and cold holding. Inspector will follow up to see that these practices are being addressed.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Food service employees were observed to enter the kitchen, don gloves, and begin handling foods without first washing hands. Provided some education, but PIC should review when to wash hands with staff.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, and prior to putting on gloves. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee observed to wash hands, then turn the faucet off without using a barrier to prevent recontamination of clean hands. CORRECTED- Provided education. Ensure employees use a paper towel or other barrier to turn the faucet off after washing hands.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment: Food employee observed to use bare hands to place a pickle on a plate. Discussed preventing bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat foods. CORRECTED- Pickle was discarded and employee used tongs to put a pickle on the plate. PIC should review glove use and preventing bare-hand contact with RTE foods with all food employees.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11 (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket observed to have no measurable concentration of quat sanitizer. CORRECTED- Bucket was emptied and new sanitizer solution was prepared (200ppm quat).
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in the cooler under the grill observed to be 49-57F (probed). Foods included cheeses, cheese sauce, steak, and ham. Out of temperature food were voluntarily discarded.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Cooler under the grill observed holding food at 49-57F (probed). Ambient thermometers inside the cooler read 65F and 45F. Cooler door requires intention to close and may easily be left open unintentionally, which could contribute to cold holding issues. Repair cooler so that foods are held at 41F or below. 
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Ambient thermometers in the cooler under the grill observed to read 45F and 65F. Foods in the cooler observed to be 49-57F. Ensure ambient thermometers are accurate. Calibrate or replace thermometers.
4-203.12: (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be accurate to +/- 1.5C. (B) accurate to +/- 3 Fahrenheit.  [Pf]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Cook was observed chewing gum while working in the kitchen. Gum was discarded at request of inspector.
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Spatulas removed from the dish machine were dried with a used, damp wiping cloth. Proper air drying of utensils and equipment after ware washing was discussed. Wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen storage. Spatulas were placed through additional ware washing cycle prior to setting aside to air dry. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solutions in sani-buckets in kitchen and front service area were a 100ppm. Fresh solutions were provided at 200ppm. Staff were advised to consider pre-wetting wiping cloths with sanitizer prior to placing in fresh solutions as sometimes wiping cloths will draw sanitizer out of solution depending on the type of cloth.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 TCS foods in the kitchen prep cooler had internal temperatures at 45F/above. Pasta salad and cantaloupe in the bottom of the cooler were observed with internal temperature of 62F and 49F-50F respectively. Products were discarded. Other foods had internal temperatures of 45F-47F in the top and bottom of the cooler, including diced/sliced tomatoes, feta cheese, sour cream portion, and chicken salad portions. Cooler was holding around 43F per inspector’s calibrated food thermometers. Benefit of doubt for foods at 45F-47F was given based on foods just being restocked and being in and out of the cooler for food service. TCS foods with internal temperatures above 45F at the close of business were to be discarded. See general comments for additional information.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112 Thermometer in the bottom of the prep cooler was reading around 30F, and the cooler was holding at 43F. New hanging thermometers were provided.
Cold holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Small coolers used for milk storage in cabinets at coffee counter had severely torn gaskets. Replace the gaskets as soon as possible. The torn gaskets in combination with staff being in and out resulted in the specialty milk cooler holding at 44F. All milks should be stored in the 2 door drink cooler by the ice machine overnight until the gaskets are replaced to allow for consistent cold holding at 41F/below.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Food service employees were observed putting on gloves to prepare and handle food without first washing hands. 
1. Cook went between various tasks, including but not limited to opening boxes to put away bread in the freezer and touching an iPad to check an online order, prior to putting on gloves to prepare a food order.
2. Front of house employee was observed handling a personal beverage prior to putting on a glove to get products out of the dessert case for customers.
Handwashing was discussed with staff during inspection, and proper handwashing between tasks was observed for the remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, and prior to putting on gloves.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Kitchen handwashing sink was used as a dump sink to discard old sanitizer solution. Proper use of the handwashing sink was discussed with the cook. Ensure handwashing sinks are not used as dump sinks.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Slices of quiche removed from the original packaging were observed sitting in direct contact with the lids of packaging. Cook was advised on storage in the original packaging or with a proper barrier between unpackaged food and the general/outer surfaces of packaging. Outer packaging is not considered a clean surface and should never be in direct contact with unwrapped foods. 
2. Pans of diced tomatoes were stacked in the top of the prep cooler so the bottom of one container was in direct contact with tomato in the pan below. Also, a pan of olives was sitting in direct contact with cheese shreds in another container in the bottom of the prep cooler. Portions of diced tomatoes and cheese shreds were discarded prior to proper storage. The bottom surfaces of containers are not considered clean and should not be stacked in direct contact with unwrapped foods. Provide lids or plastic wrap to allow for separation between the bottoms of containers and the food in other containers when products are stacked. 
3. Pan of cheese shreds from the bottom of the prep cooler was briefly set on the floor while another food item was removed from the cooler to prepare an order. Cheese shreds were placed in a new container, and the pan that touched the floor was taken to the dish area for ware washing. Cease the practice of placing pans of food on the floor when obtaining products from coolers.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in kitchen sani-bucket was at 100ppm. Cook just started their shift at 2pm and noted it was probably from use earlier in the day prior to their arrival. Fresh solution was provided at 200ppm. Ensure sani-buckets are changed as needed throughout daily operations, including at shift changes.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Cut cantaloupe in the top of the prep cooler had surface temperatures of 52F-53F. Pieces of cantaloupe in the container had internal temperatures ranging from 49F-53F. Container holding cantaloupe was stored at an angle and positioned within a smaller container in the top of the cooler, so the cantaloupe was not in direct contact with cold air. Cantaloupe was placed in the freezer to quickly chill prior to storage in the bottom of the prep cooler.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 1. Open bags of arugula and spinach in the 2 door cooler were without date marks. Date marks were provided. Ensure proper date marking of leafy greens once packages are opened.
2. Open carton of heavy whipping cream was without a date mark in the reach-in cooler under the grill. Carton was almost empty and was discarded. 
3. Pans with portions of rice and other prepared foods were observed with date marks of 5/11. Portions of products were frozen and just pulled for thawing as of today. Label was changed to reflect proper date when products were pulled from the freezer. 
4. Chicken salad dressing prepared the day prior was without a date mark in the glass front reach-in cooler. Container had a piece of tape on it, but the date was never written down. Date mark was provided during inspection.
5. Portion of cooked, chopped chicken was observed with a date mark of 5/10 in the bottom of the glass front reach-in cooler. Cook noted the product was frozen on 5/10 and pulled from the freezer the day prior to thaw for use. Proper date mark was provided. 
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Unlabeled spray bottle of pink colored liquid was observed at the front service counter. Another bottle with what appeared to be the same chemical was labeled as all purpose cleaner. Staff confirmed the unlabeled bottle contained all purpose cleaner and provided a proper label. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 1. Bags of ice were observed on the floor in the walk-in freezer. Cook noted bagged ice was purchased for use when the ice machine was broken over the weekend. Proper storage up off the floor was discussed.
1. Box of tortilla shells was observed on the the floor under shelving in the walk-in cooler, and boxes of chicken breasts were on the floor by the door inside the walk-in freezer. Both products were said to be received in a delivery earlier that day. Boxes of chicken breasts were moved to allow for proper storage on a racks in the freezer. Ensure box of tortilla shells gets moved to allow for proper storage up off the floor. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 1. Damp wiping cloth was observed sitting in front of the slicer. Cook noted it was likely being used for cleaning by another employee prior to shift change. Wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen storage bag. 
2. Inspector later observed another damp wiping cloth sitting out after surfaces were wiped down in the kitchen. 
Ensure wiping cloths are properly stored between uses.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Cook with manager’s certification has not completed a food allergen course to obtain certification. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee at service counter was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing was discussed. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of a forearm or elbow to shut off a faucet would also be acceptable.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 Cook was observed having barehand contact with spinach. Spinach in question was discarded. Proper use of barriers to minimize barehand contact was discussed. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables or when ingredients will be added to food that is being fully cooked/has a kill step for pathogens, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Cook was observed using a wiping cloth to wipe the stem of the probe food thermometer. The wiping cloth in question was hanging from their apron and said to be used for handling hot trays and pans. Wiping cloth in question was placed in soiled linen storage. Probe of food thermometer was properly wiped with an alcohol wipe prior to storage. 
2. Open, cut portion of avocado was observed sitting in direct contact with packaging of sealed avocado portions. Cooks were advised on storage of open portions of avocado with a proper barrier. Outer packaging is not considered a clean surface and should never be in direct contact with unwrapped foods. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 1. Quat solutions in sanitizer-buckets at the front service counter were observed at 100ppm. Hot water was being used to prepare solutions at the 3 part sink dispenser. Proper use of cool water to prepare sanitizer was discussed. Preparation of solutions with cool water resulted in a concentration of 200ppm.
2. Sani-bucket in the pastry prep area was observed to be soiled and at a concentration of 0ppm. Employee working in the area noted it was prepared around 6am. Employee was in the middle of working with food and stated the solution would be changed as soon as they were done with the task at hand. Ensure solutions are changed frequently throughout operations and maintained at proper concentration.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 1. Open bags of arugula and spinach in the 2 door cooler were without date marks. Arugula and spinach were discarded and replaced with fresh product. Date marking of open packages was discussed.
2. Open carton of heavy whipping cream was with other a date mark. Carton was said to be opened the day prior and dated accordingly.
3. Pans with portions of rice and other prepared foods were observed with date marks of 12/8. Labels were incorrect and should have said 1/8. Products in question were pulled from the freezer for use as of 1/8. Proper date marks were provided.
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottles without labels were observed on a bottom shelf in the kitchen. Cook noted the spray bottles were not used by kitchen staff. Staff were unsure as to the contents, but the bottles appeared to contain soap. Solutions were discarded during inspection. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Employee working in dish area did not have a food handler certification. One of the cooks and a front service employee did not have copies of current certifications. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Ensure food handler course is completed within 30 days fo hiring. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were cited during the inspection. See violations 15, 16, & 20 for details. Sanitizer was not connected to the dish machine at the time of inspection, and facility did not have dish machine sanitizer available for use. Signed employee health reporting agreements were also not available for newer employees working at the time of inspection. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the re-inspection. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 Signed reporting agreements were not available for newer employees. Employee health policy was discussed with new GM, and employees working at the time of inspection signed copies of the reporting agreement. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Sani-bucket was emptied in the front service counter handwashing sink. Employee was advised on proper use of handwashing sinks. Handwashing sinks should not be used as a dump sink.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee handled a writing utensil and touched general surfaces with gloved hands and then proceeded to handling clean equipment to reassemble the slicer while wearing the same pair of gloves. Proper glove use was discussed, and gloves were discarded. Ensure glove changes occur as needed. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Food contact surface of ice scoop was observed touching the wall where drywall was damaged and general discoloration was observed next to the ice machine. The edge of the ice scoop and moisture caused damaged over time to the wall behind the ice scoop storage rack. Ice scoop holder was removed from the wall, and the ice scoop was taken to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. The ice scoop will be stored in a clean container on top of the ice machine until repairs are made to allow for proper storage. Ensure the ice scoop and storage container are cleaned at the end of operations daily and more frequently if potential contamination occurs.
 Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Knives and and cooking utensils were soiled with food debris in the kitchen. When cleaning frequency was discussed, manager indicated the utensils get cleaned once or twice a day. Cleaning frequency should be up to every 4hrs after continuous use, and utensils in question had been in use for an unknown amount of time. All utensils were taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
If used with time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4hrs.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine was observed with a final rinse concentration of 10ppm. Detergent was connected to the sanitizer chemical line. Sanitizer was not available and had to be ordered. Sanitizer line was primed after connecting a gallon of bleach to the machine, and a concentration of 100ppm was observed.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling
Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

Quat solutions in sanitizer-buckets at the front service counter were observed at 0ppm and 100ppm. Fresh sanitizer solutions were provided at 200ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Chicken breasts cooked this morning had internal temperatures of 48F to 62F. Chicken breasts were cooled on baking sheets in the walk-in cooler starting around 10am, but internal temperatures were not monitored during the process. Chicken breasts were discarded during inspection.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle at the front counter had a pinkish red liquid in it and was labeled as sanitizer. The solution tested at 0ppm with a quat test strip. The chemical was correctly identified by staff as all purpose cleaner, and the bottle was re-labeled during inspection. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-901.11 Employee working in dish area was observed using a cloth towel to dry plates. Employee was advised to cease the practice of using towels to dry equipment and utensils. All equipment and utensils are required to air dry after going through ware washing process.
After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining as specified in the first paragraph of the first paragraph of 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), before contact with food; and (B) may not be cloth dried except that utensils that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are maintained clean and dry.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-501.15 Dish machine had two containers of dish detergent hooked up, with one connected to the detergent chemical line and the other connected to the sanitizer chemical line. The detergent connected to the sanitizer line was yellow in color and was assumed to be sanitizer prior to observing a detergent label. Bleach was provided until correct sanitizer arrives with the scheduled delivery tomorrow. Ensure proper chemicals are available and connected to the correct chemical tubing.
A warewashing machine and its auxiliary components shall be operated in accordance with the machine's data plate and other manufacturer's instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Violation remains to be corrected by the next routine inspection. See 7/1/21 routine inspection report for details.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were cited during the inspection (see 8 & 16 for details). PIC and staff were unaware the wall mounted chemical dispenser at the 3 part sink was not dispensing sanitizer at proper concentration, and two of the sani-buckets were filled using the 3 part sink dispenser. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the re-inspection. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 Signed reporting agreements were not available for newer employees that just started at the facility. Employee health policy was discussed, and employees working at the time of inspection signed copies of the reporting agreement. PIC noted a list of remaining employees that need to sign was created to ensure all other new staff also review and sign the reporting agreement. All other persons working had copies of signed reporting agreements available. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee at front service counter was observed drinking from a personal beverage and touched the straw up near their mouth. Employee did not wash hands prior to removing a beverage container from the 2 door cooler. Employee was advised on handwashing between tasks, including after drinking from a personal beverage. Employees at front service area were observed washing hands between tasks for the remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after eating or drinking, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Slicer was observed with buildup of food debris on the back surface just beneath the blade. Cook stated the push block and blade were removed and ran through the dish machine after use that morning. Slicer was disassembled to allow for proper cleaning and sanitization of the back surface. Ensure all slicer food contact surfaces that cannot be taken to the dish area for ware washing and manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized. 
--Tongs hanging at the door of the kitchen oven were soiled with food debris. Cook noted tongs in question were not used recently. Tongs were taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
--Can opener had food debris stuck on the blade. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized, 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 One sani-bucket at the front service counter and one in the kitchen were observed with a concentration of 0ppm quat. Sani-buckets were filled using the wall mounted chemical dispenser at the 3 part sink. Sanitizer was not suctioning properly at the 3 part sink dispenser. All solutions were replaced with fresh solution from the dispenser in the chemical closet and observed at 200ppm. PIC called for service during the inspection (see general comments for details). In the meantime, all quat solutions need to be prepared using the dispenser in the chemical closet. Ensure all staff are aware of the need to fill sani-buckets at the mopsink dispenser until the 3 part sink dispenser is repaired. 

Sanitizer in a spray bottle at the front service counter was observed at 100ppm quat. Fresh solution was provided. Ensure spray bottles of sanitizer are checked with test strips to verify concentration and refreshed as needed prior to concentration becoming weak and ineffective. 

A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the 
manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Boxes of chicken breasts and turkey burgers were stored on the floor in the walkin freezer. PIC placed boxes on a cart to allow for proper storage. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
